## America’s Car-Mart Secures $60 million in New Capital and Committed Buyer to Strengthen Business and Continue Serving Customers


November 24, 2026


*The Company to complete sale transaction and reduce debt through court-supervised sale transaction*


*Dealerships remain open for account servicing and customers should keep making payments the same way and on the same schedule as usual*


*Under the proposed Plan, which is subject to Court approval, trade creditors would be paid in full*


*The ACMAT securitization trusts are not debtors in the Chapter 11 cases, and the Company is seeking Court authority to continue servicing the securitized receivables held by the trusts in the ordinary course*


ROGERS, Ark., Nov. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- America’s Car-Mart, Inc. (NASDAQ: CRMT) (“Car-Mart” or the “Company”), today announced that the Company has entered into an asset purchase agreement to sell substantially all of the Company’s assets to Cardinal Asset Holdings LLC and certain of its affiliates (collectively, “Cardinal Holdings” or the “Buyer”), a well-capitalized ownership group led by a deeply experienced executive team that collectively has more than 100 years leading companies in the automotive retail and consumer finance industries. The parties intend to implement the transaction through a pre-packaged Chapter 11 process. Accordingly, today the Company and certain of its subsidiaries filed petitions to restructure under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas (the “Court”). The Company also filed a proposed pre-packaged Chapter 11 plan (the “Plan”) that, among other things, proposes to pay general unsecured claims in full. The Plan remains subject to Court approval.


The announcement follows a comprehensive review of strategic alternatives led by the Special Committee of the Company's board of directors, with the goal of maximizing value for all stakeholders and ensuring the continuation of the essential services Car-Mart provides to its customers. Prior to filing, the Company’s advisors conducted a robust marketing process that engaged a broad range of potential strategic and financial parties.


Cardinal Holdings, whose leadership includes a former Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of America's Car-Mart and executives with decades of experience in automotive retail and consumer finance, will serve as the “stalking horse” bidder, setting the value floor for the sale process, while giving other potential buyers the opportunity to come forward with higher or better offers.


“Over the past several months, our Special Committee and board have worked through the full range of options available to us. This transaction provides a committed buyer for the business and the financing to rebuild our inventory,” said Doug Campbell, Chief Executive Officer. “With this new capital, we are restocking our lots ahead of tax season, so our customers will find a wider selection of vehicles and we can welcome more new customers through our doors. Our associates have carried this company through a difficult year, and they continue to show up for our customers and for each other. We are grateful for their dedication.”


"We believe strongly in Car-Mart and the opportunity to build on its more than four decades of serving customers and communities," said Chad Melchi, a principal of Cardinal Holdings. "Car-Mart has a trusted brand, a loyal customer base, and a dedicated team. We’re grateful for the associates who have stood by this business during a difficult period, and we see real opportunity ahead for the people who will build the Company’s next chapter with us. Our group brings significant financial capital and a leadership team with deep experience operating and growing successful businesses in consumer finance and automotive retail, including buy here, pay here, and we plan to continue the restocking now underway so customers have more vehicles to choose from. We look forward to working through the Court-supervised process and completing the transaction."


Throughout the process, America’s Car-Mart’s dealerships will remain open and will continue to serve its communities. The Company will continue servicing accounts as they have throughout Car-Mart’s review of strategic alternatives, and customers should keep making payments the same way and on the same schedule as usual. Customers' vehicle service contracts and accident protection plans remain in place, and the Company has asked the Court for approval to continue these and other customer programs as usual. The Company's ACMAT securitization trusts, which are separate special-purpose entities sponsored by America’s Car-Mart, are not debtors in the Chapter 11 cases. The ACMAT notes are obligations of the applicable issuing trust, and payable from the receivables and other assets held by that trust, are not general obligations of, or guaranteed by, America’s Car-Mart. The Company has asked the Court for authority to continue servicing the securitized receivables held by the trusts and remitting collections to the applicable trust accounts in the ordinary course. Questions about noteholder rights or other matters under the securitization documents should be directed to the indenture trustee. America’s Car-Mart cannot provide investment advice, and holders are encouraged to consult with their financial and legal advisors before making any decision regarding their holdings.


The Company has filed customary motions with the Court seeking authority to continue operating in the ordinary course, including to continue paying employees’ wages and benefits, honoring customer programs, and continuing to service customer accounts, including securitized accounts. With the new capital being provided, the Company expects to have sufficient resources to continue to pay vendors and suppliers in the ordinary course throughout the Chapter 11 process. Under the Plan, which is subject to Court approval, trade creditors would be paid in full in the ordinary course of business. In addition, the Plan contemplates $2.5 million for equity holders to be funded from the monetization of select assets excluded from the proposed sale transaction to the Buyer under the asset purchase agreement, with additional potential recovery to equity holders from the residual value, if any, in the proposed sale transaction. However, there can be no assurance that the transactions contemplated by the Plan will result in proceeds being available to distribute to common stockholders in the amount contemplated, or at all, after the Company’s creditors are paid in full.


All documents filed in the Chapter 11 cases can be obtained free of charge on the case website maintained by the Company’s claims and noticing agent, Omni Agent Solutions, Inc.,[https://omniagentsolutions.com/ACM](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=HYVT3fRYUVxsIKV4cGhWwtCvquGcBxiB7Q7-YYZpxi7x7qufEFdcW2dJt-Gab1DK4SAfofPmQnNdeimg9jOrZ0eN81Juof9WC-5MCfSOdCigpQDgnFo5oEDgKlFflVZW) or by calling at 866-205-3145 (U.S. and Canada) or 818-793-5130 (International).


The Company is advised by Mayer Brown LLP as legal counsel, Houlihan Lokey Capital, Inc. as investment banker, and FTI Consulting as financial advisor. Cardinal Holdings is advised by Troutman Pepper Locke LLP as legal counsel and Stephens Inc. as investment banker.


**About America’s Car-Mart, Inc.**
America’s Car-Mart operates automotive dealerships in 12 states and is one of the largest publicly held automotive retailers in the United States focused exclusively on the “Integrated Auto Sales and Finance” segment of the used car market. The Company emphasizes superior customer service and the building of strong personal relationships with its customers. The Company operates its dealerships primarily in smaller cities throughout the South-Central United States, selling quality used vehicles and providing financing for substantially all its customers. For more information about America’s Car-Mart, please visit our website at[www.car-mart.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=mjDRpWXkntGWQCEMdDi3iscrFIRW2Q9-gQwTxRfqbG-cFlACXfMVWJ145vOLXbFZK8EN9pK1d-9qmcXCHTgoqwDQQtIdHvpzvZpgav-Es4k=) .


**About Cardinal Holdings**
Cardinal Holdings is a privately held investment group formed to acquire and operate America's Car-Mart. Its leadership includes Chad Melchi, a 20-year chief executive in buy here, pay here auto retail; Tilman J. "Skip" Falgout III, former Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of America's Car-Mart; Ted Saunders, Chief Executive Officer of Snap Finance; and Robert Hennessy of the Atlanta family behind Hennessy Automobile Companies.
